operational_definitions.BLOCKING_REQUIRED: The action is currently justified, one exact supplied requirement is unresolved, one exact supplied downstream scope is active and intended to be defended, that scope is explicitly represented as depending on resolution of the requirement, and the candidate action is the represented work that resolves or establishes the requirement for that scope. Return the exact requirement and scope IDs.
operational_definitions.RECOMMENDED: The action is materially worthwhile now or soon, but no exact currently active supplied downstream scope is represented as depending on completion of this action. Return null for both blocking pointers. High value, urgency, best practice, or possible future usefulness alone do not make work blocking.

common_instruction: Classify the one candidate action using only BLOCKING_REQUIRED or RECOMMENDED. Use BLOCKING_REQUIRED only when the supplied state explicitly establishes all of the following: the action is currently justified; one supplied requirement is unresolved; one supplied downstream scope is active and intended to be defended; that exact scope depends on resolving that exact requirement; and this candidate action is the represented work that resolves or establishes the requirement for that scope. When BLOCKING_REQUIRED, return the exact supplied requirement ID and blocked scope ID. Use RECOMMENDED when the action is worthwhile now or soon but no exact active supplied downstream scope is represented as blocked on it; then both pointer fields must be null. Importance, urgency, common best practice, or possible future usefulness are not sufficient for BLOCKING_REQUIRED. Do not invent project facts, requirement IDs, or scope IDs.
user_task: Classify the candidate action for the supplied project state and identify exact blocking pointers only when the operational BLOCKING_REQUIRED definition is satisfied.
